$comment: ALL 679 currently-active Ohio municipal income tax jurisdictions (this $comment previously said 678, off by one from municipalityCount and the array's own length below -- corrected 2026-09-02), sourced directly from the Ohio Dept of Taxation's own official Finder database (bulk CSV, not hand-searched/transcribed). This replaces the earlier 3-anchor-city approach in this file with real, primary-sourced comprehensive coverage -- genuinely comparable in depth to what a competitor like Symmetry would maintain for Ohio.

source.title: Ohio Municipal Income Tax Rates (The Finder, bulk CSV download)
source.downloadedBy: fetched directly via curl this session -- this is the SAME authoritative feed Ohio's own Finder tool uses, not a secondary aggregator
source.method: Filtered to rows with EffEndDate=99991231 (currently open-ended / in force). Historical superseded rates (404 additional rows) were excluded, not deleted -- available by re-fetching the same URL and keeping earlier rows if effective-dated history is ever needed.
source.rateFormat: Rate is a fraction (e.g. 0.025 = 2.5%), matching the source CSV's own convention -- no conversion applied.

taxableWages.basis: Ohio municipal 'qualifying wages' (ORC 718.01(R)): Medicare wages under IRC 3121(a), less Section 125 cafeteria-plan amounts, with 401(k), 403(b) and 457 employee deferrals added back. This is NOT the Ohio state income tax base: an elective retirement deferral reduces Ohio state (and school district) taxable income but does not reduce the municipal base.
taxableWages.exemptPretaxComment: Mirrors the federal Medicare list (data/federal/2026.json medicare.exemptPretax): section125/hsa/fsa/dependent_care are cafeteria-plan amounts ORC 718.01(R)(1)(a) deducts, and qualified transportation fringes (commuter) are excluded from 3121(a) wages by 3121(a)(20) with no ORC add-back. deferral_401k/403b/457/simple are deliberately absent: 3121(a) already includes them and (R)(2)(c) adds back any 401(k)/403(b)/457 amount not included.

sources.title: Ohio Revised Code 718.01(R), definition of "qualifying wages"
sources.quote: "Qualifying wages" means wages, as defined in section 3121(a) of the Internal Revenue Code, without regard to any wage limitations, adjusted as follows: (1) Deduct ... (a) Any amount included in wages if the amount constitutes compensation attributable to a plan or program described in section 125 ... (2) Add ... (c) Any amount not included in wages if the amount is an amount described in section 401(k), 403(b), or 457 of the Internal Revenue Code. Division (R)(2)(c) of this section applies only to employee contributions and employee deferrals.

residencyNote: Ohio municipal income tax is primarily workplace-sourced: this single rate generally applies to income earned within the municipality regardless of the earner's residence (unlike Michigan's explicit resident/nonresident split). ohioLocalTax() (src/taxes/state.ts) implements the ORC 718.121 resident-credit-against-work-city at withholding time -- a resident working in a DIFFERENT taxing municipality gets that home municipality's tax reduced by the tax paid to the work municipality, capped at the home rate, verified end-to-end in tests/engine.test.ts.
confidence: primary_source_confirmed for every row -- downloaded directly from Ohio's own database, not cross-referenced from secondary sites. This is a STRONGER confidence tier than the per-city web-search approach used for 21 of Michigan's 24 cities, because it is bulk-sourced from the authority itself rather than corroborated across secondary summaries.

ohioLocalTax() implements the ORC 718.121 resident-city-vs-work-city credit at withholding time — the home municipality's tax is reduced by the tax paid to the work municipality, capped at the home rate. Verified: working in Columbus while living in Cleveland produces one $75.00 line rather than two.

JEDD/JEDZ zones are a SEPARATE dataset -- see data/local/OH-jedd-jedz-2026.json -- because they are legally distinct (contractual zones, not municipalities) and use a different ID scheme in Ohio's own data.

This is a snapshot as of the fetch date; Ohio's own CSV is the living source of truth and should be re-fetched periodically (harvester territory, Phase 9) rather than this file treated as permanently current.

administeringAgencies.$comment: NEW this session: WHO an employer actually remits municipal withholding to. Ohio municipalities do not uniformly collect their own tax the way Michigan's 24 cities do -- many contract with a regional third-party agency. This is a real operational fact a payroll company needs (where to send the money and file the return), separate from the rate itself.

administeringAgencies.knownDataGap: 5 RITA/CCA member municipalities were NOT found anywhere in this file's 679-municipality list after name normalization: ["DeGraff","Germantown","North Hampton","Stockport","Valleyview (Franklin)"]. RE-CHECKED 2026-09-02 against a fresh pull of the same Finder CSV this file is built from (thefinder.tax.ohio.gov's own municipal rate download, 685 unique municipality codes as of this pull vs. this file's 679): DeGraff, North Hampton, and Stockport are CONFIRMED still genuinely absent from Finder itself, not just from this file's parse -- Ohio's own database has no rate row for any of the three under that name. Germantown and Valleyview, however, ARE present in the fresh CSV -- the original 'genuinely absent' claim for those two was imprecise. The real, different problem: Germantown's most recent row is $.015 effective 2019-01-01 but EXPIRES 2025-12-31 (MuniCode 29932), and Valleyview's is $.01 effective 2012-01-01 but EXPIRES 2017-12-31 (MuniCode 79282) -- both with no successor row as of this pull, meaning either the levy genuinely lapsed (some Ohio villages tax via a renewable, time-limited voter levy) or Finder simply hasn't posted a renewal yet. Deliberately NOT added with either the expired rate or a guessed continuation -- adding a rate that may no longer be legally in effect would be a worse error than the current $0/no-line outcome, and this project's own standing rule is to disclose an ambiguity rather than guess through it. Whether Germantown's/Valleyview's levies are still active needs a source Finder's CSV itself doesn't resolve (each village's own current ordinance or the county auditor), not a re-parse of this same pipeline. This means the municipality COUNT (679) is a genuine undercount by 3 confirmed-real, currently-unlisted municipalities (DeGraff/North Hampton/Stockport) plus 2 more (Germantown/Valleyview) whose CURRENT rate is unconfirmed rather than confirmed-zero.
